subject: Clarifying questions: Private deployment security & operator scoping (Arbiter PH)
body:
Message 1:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@arbiterph.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Jamie Lin <jamie.lin@arbiterph.com>, procurement@arbiterph.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Arbiter RFP: follow-up questions on private deployment

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the RFP packet — a few quick clarifications from our infrastructure and security teams before we proceed to the technical deep-dive:

1) Operator access model: In the sealed/private deployment, can Redwood run a vendor-managed operator process, or do you require a customer-only operator model? If both are supported, what separation controls exist?

2) KMS integration: Do you support external HSMs (PKCS#11) / customer-managed KMS for secrets at rest and for image signing? Any constraints on algorithms (e.g., FIPS 140-2/3)?

3) Offline patching and upgrades: For air-gapped installs, what is your recommended patch bundle process and how long is the maximum offline window you support between critical security patches?

4) Audit logs & evidence: Does Redwood retain detailed operator action logs (sudo/CLI/API) locally? Can logs be configured to ship to a customer SIEM in the absence of outbound network access?

We can accept a short bulleted response and any reference attachments (network diagram / runbook / compliance addendum).

Best,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Infrastructure, Arbiter Pharmaceuticals
alex.morgan@arbiterph.com

---
Message 2:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@arbiterph.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Arbiter RFP: follow-up questions on private deployment

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; attached are the technical matrix and operator runbook you requested (short stubs included). Happy to hop on a call for any of these.

1) Operator access model
- Supported modes: (a) Customer-managed operators only (default), (b) Vendor-managed operators via a limited-scope operator bundle (by exception on dedicated contracts).
- Separation controls: role-based operator accounts, RBAC for operator actions, two-person approval for critical operations (e.g., cluster rekey, certificate roll). All operator commands are logged with request/response snapshots.
- Recommendation for Arbiter: we typically deliver an initial onboarding bundle where Redwood engineers lead the first-week deployments under a scoped SOW; handoff to customer operators is performed within the first 10 business days with training and runbook sign-off.

2) KMS integration
- We support direct integration with customer KMS/HSM via PKCS#11 and cloud KMS APIs (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS).
- FIPS: Our supported crypto stack can be configured to operate in FIPS mode when using FIPS-validated HSMs/KMS endpoints. We document required algorithms and policy settings in the attached tech matrix.
- Image signing: We support customer-side image signing and verification at deploy time; signing keys can remain behind customer KMS/HSM.

3) Offline patching and upgrades
- Air-gapped process: patches are packaged as discrete signed bundles (patch bundle format documented in runbook). Customer pulls bundles via removable media or an approved internal transfer mechanism.
- Recommended maximum offline window: we advise no more than 60 days for non-critical patches; critical security patches should be applied within 14 days where possible. If constraints require longer windows, we provide compensating hardening guidance and an emergency hotfix procedure.

4) Audit logs & evidence
- Operator action logging: yes — detailed CLI/API operator audit events, including command arguments, actor identity, and pre/post snapshots are stored locally in write-once append logs.
- SIEM forwarding: we can ship logs to customer SIEMs via file export, SFTP push, or (where permitted) direct syslog/HTTPS forwarders. For fully air-gapped installs we provide signed log bundles and a log collection tool in the operator runbook.

Attachments included:
- redwood_private_deploy_tech_matrix_v1.xlsx (capabilities, crypto list, required kernel modules)
- redwood_operator_runbook_v1.pdf (onboarding, patch bundle process, operator commands)
- network_topology_arbiter.png (example network diagram with egress control points)

Next steps: if the answers above align, we can schedule a technical workshop with our deployments engineering and your security team next week. Please propose 2x 60-minute slots.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Message 3:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@arbiterph.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Jamie Lin <jamie.lin@arbiterph.com>, procurement@arbiterph.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Arbiter RFP: follow-up questions on private deployment

Thanks Priya — that was helpful. Two quick follow-ups from our security lead:

- Audit log retention: is there a default retention period for local operator logs and can it be extended indefinitely by the customer (we would prefer 7 years for certain regulated actions)?
- Operator privileges: can RBAC be scoped to support temporary elevation (e.g., time-bound sudo) and do you emit attestations for elevation events?

Appreciate a short response and any reference to where those are documented.

Best,
Alex

---
Message 4:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@arbiterph.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 15:38:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Arbiter RFP: follow-up questions on private deployment

Hi Alex — following up on the two items from your security lead. Short answers below and attaching our audit retention addendum for regulated retention scenarios.

- Audit log retention: default local retention is 180 days in the packaged deploy (configurable). Customers can configure log export and long-term archival; we provide a signed export tool that prepares tamper-evident log bundles for import into long-term storage. For regulated workflows, we support retention policies up to 10 years (7 years is supported) when customer manages archival. See attached: audit_log_retention_addendum_v1.pdf.

- Operator privileges & elevation: RBAC supports time-bound elevation tokens and just-in-time elevation workflows via a built-in approval flow or integration with customer IGA (Okta, SailPoint). Elevation events are recorded and we emit a signed attestation (SHA256) for any elevation which can be stored alongside the audit bundle.

If you want, we can add a short appendix to the runbook that shows a sample JIT elevation request and the exact attestation format. We can include that in the workshop materials.

Thanks — I copied Laura for policy and will await your proposed workshop times.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.example.com

[Attachment: audit_log_retention_addendum_v1.pdf (PDF)]
